about:
Laurel Wire Company, Inc. was founded in 1983 in Plainville, Connecticut, by Dick Clark and his business partner William Killiany. At just 27 years old, Clark started the business in his garage on Laurel Street with a focus on wire straightening and cutting services.

The company specializes in precision wire straightening and cutting for round and strip materials, handling diameters from 0.030 to 0.364 inches and lengths up to 40 feet depending on alloy and temper. It also provides through-feed centerless grinding services. Laurel Wire purchases all raw material and processes it to customer specifications, serving both prototype and large-scale production needs.

Its customer base spans automotive, aerospace, industrial, and consumer sectors. Components produced by Laurel Wire are used in heat exchangers, jewelry, springs, fishing lures, tubing mandrels, acoustical ceilings, pipe organs, bookbinding, extension drills, hinges, wire forms, heating elements, and Swiss screw machining applications.

Clark founded the company on a passionate commitment to the customer, a principle that remains central. The firm emphasizes customizable material, length, size, and temper options, proactive communication throughout projects, and a quality-first approach that it says distinguishes it from competitors.
